reason: Ruby `Array#reject!` mutates the receiver in place; `extractBang` removes the extracted elements from the same array with a reverse `splice` loop, the only in-place removal JS offers. Surfaced by the DescendantsTracker `reject!` port making the name resolvable, not by a change in this file.

Ruby `size.div number` is Integer#div, floor division as a METHOD (grouping.rb:66). JS has no method form for it — `Math.floor(array.length / n)` (array-utils.ts:94) is the whole of it — so the call cannot survive the port.
Ruby's `Array.new(padding, fill_with)` (grouping.rb:38) builds the pad run; JS spells the same allocation as an array literal/`fill`, with no constructor call to match.
